correctness.rationale: Exact sign transformation converts SDP gain to one positive endpoint chord term minus weighted path chord energies. Weighted Cauchy gives the exact threshold and forces a unique critical Gram matrix. Spherical geodesic shortening reduces every global candidate to a planar shortest path; convex local path cost yields b_j sin(delta_j)=lambda. The stationary equation has a unique positive near-threshold branch by its negative cubic coefficient D/6>0, and critical compactness excludes distant optimizers. Envelope differentiation gives gap coefficient 3 S^4/[4(S^3-T)] and a uniform remainder for every fixed positive weight profile. Independent standard-library bisection examples reproduce exact rational coefficients; finite tests are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The scalar threshold alone describes exact versus inexact solutions but not the quantitative loss of the relaxation certificate under infinitesimal edge-weight perturbation. The first nonzero exact curvature uses both the reciprocal first and third moments, yields a square-root optimizer-angle bifurcation, and proves a sharp heterogeneity penalty at fixed effective path resistance. This is a natural optimization-sensitivity invariant for a canonical nonuniform cycle family rather than a single arbitrary numerical instance. The coefficient can grow without bound as the fixed-threshold profile degenerates.
